title: Nairobi to host ‘historic’ 2029 World Athletics Championships as London misses out
content:
The 2029 World Athletics Championships will be hosted in Nairobi, Kenya, marking the first time that the event will be staged on the African continent.

It means that London will miss out on hosting the event that last came to the British capital in 2017, while the 2031 edition has been given to Munich, Germany.

The decision was announced in the Hungarian capital Budapest on Tuesday, after the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships.

“Athletics is woven into the fabric of Kenya,” World Athletics president Sebastian Coe said on a media call.

Coe, in his final year of presidency, explained that the sport’s governing body is “determined to connect with audiences worldwide,” and referenced the popularity of athletics there. He said that Nairobi and Munich are “very different but exciting opportunities for our sport” and will see “two groundbreaking championships”.

“Taking our championships to Africa for the first time will be historic,” Coe added of an event which was inaugurated in 1983 and, since 1991, has been held biannually in odd-numbered years. Five years ago, Kenya hosted the world under-20 championships, and in 2017 they staged the under-18 equivalent.

“Nairobi has presented a compelling and an emotional bid,” the World Athletics president added, name-checking the likes of Faith Kipyegon, Eliud Kipchoge and David Rudisha, all Olympic gold medallists and middle/long-distance athletes who have held world records.

“The level of fan engagement in Kenya is extraordinary,” Coe continued. “According to Nielsen Research, Kenya is the single-most interested market in athletics, with 68 per cent of Kenyans rating their interest very high against a 39 per cent global average.

“Athletics is the second-most followed sport in Kenya. Their fans ranked fourth-highest on our social media channels. It was important that the world championship should come to Africa, when we had the right host, the right bid, and the right circumstances.”

He added that Nairobi has “steadily built its credentials” by hosting youth championships, and that the multi-purpose Kasarani Stadium will be fit to host the nine-day event as it is currently undergoing renovation ahead of next year’s African Cup of Nations. That AFCON will be another historic moment, as the global continental football tournament goes to east Africa for the first time, hosted across Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

With next September’s world championships already confirmed for Beijing, China — Tuesday’s announcement means that three consecutive editions will be staged outside of Europe. There will be back-to-back hosts in east Asia, as Beijing next year follows Tokyo in 2025.

“Europe is a heartland, and we openly accept that it is in large part the breadbasket of our sport,” Coe said on failed bids for London and also Rome. “But we do also have a responsibility to make sure that an international governing federation has the opportunity to be able to take our championships into areas that, strategically, we think will actually grow the footprint of our sport.”
